answer:
Your Budget note is now a personal budget app, and it opens without errors. I haven't tried it with your real data. The preview only shows scrambled sample data, so I haven't seen the seeded numbers or the category chart on screen.

- **Month:** it has arrows to move between months. It shows spent against budget overall and per category, a "left per day" figure, and a donut chart of spending by category. Tap a category to change its budget for that month only.
- **Expenses:** the + button is on every screen. It opens a form with amount, category chips, date and note. You can edit an expense by tapping it, and delete it from the trash button with an Undo. You can search and filter by category and by month or all time, and export CSV.
- **Recurring:** rent, subscriptions and so on, each with a day of the month and an on/off switch. When you open the app in a new month, they are added to it automatically. Changing a recurring item doesn't alter expenses already added.
- **Settings:** currency, the day the month starts, and categories (add, rename, colour, default monthly budget).
- **Demo data:** August, September and October, with six recurring items and 29 one-off expenses across eight categories. September has a higher Shopping budget as an example of a per-month change.

- **CSV export:** it tries a file download and also copies the CSV to the clipboard, since I don't know whether downloads work inside the app. A toast tells you what happened.
- **Recurring items fill the whole month:** the full month's recurring expenses are added when the month starts, including ones dated later in it. They count toward spent straight away.
- **No category delete:** you can add and rename categories, but not delete them. I left delete out so existing expenses aren't left without a category.
